**Yes. A component-issue event for manufacturing order MO-25-09-1070 was created 75 minutes after the September cost period entered Pending Close, yet its recorded accounting status is `POSTED`.**

### Event identified

| Item | Finding |
|---|---|
| Work order | **MO-25-09-1070** — ID `WO-2025-09-004` |
| Operation / product | Modine Racine, Dekoven — Cooler Plate Pack |
| Source transaction | `TXN-ISSUE-250930-1070` |
| Cost event | `CE-250904-0004` |
| Event type | `INPUT` — “Component issue after pending close” |
| Amount | **USD $284,763.42** (`28,476,342` cents) |
| Cost period | `Sep-25` — `PER-COST-2025-09` |
| Exact event-created time | **`2025-09-30T19:15:00`** |
| Exact Pending Close time | **`2025-09-30T18:00:00`** |
| Time after Pending Close | **75 minutes** — 1 hour 15 minutes |
| Recorded accounting status | **`POSTED`** |

**Calculation:** `19:15:00 − 18:00:00 = 4,500 seconds ÷ 60 = 75 minutes`.

The timestamps above are reproduced exactly as stored; the records do not specify a time-zone offset.

### Policy conclusion

**The recorded `POSTED` status is not consistent with Oracle’s documented Pending Close treatment for this event.**

Oracle Fusion Cloud SCM Cost Management 26B states that newly created transactions falling in or before a Pending Close period will not be staged in Cost Accounting or Receipt Accounting and will be processed after the period is closed or reopened. It specifically states that transactions created after the Pending Close date will not be processed, even when they relate to the current or a prior period.

The documented exceptions—revenue lines, COGS recognition, and manual cost adjustments—do **not** apply to this `INPUT` component-issue event.

**Sources:** `state.db`, tables `work_orders`, `cost_periods`, and `work_order_cost_events`; supplied Oracle 26B guide, **“Cost Accounting Period Statuses and Transaction Accounting,” PDF page 233 / printed page 225**.

The review was read-only; **no database records were changed**.
